title: Nifty 50 Tests 24,100 Support as Banking Rout and Middle East Tensions Weigh on Markets
excerpt: Indian benchmarks face a third straight session of pressure as HDFC Bank's margin weakness, rising crude oil prices near $90 a barrel, and escalating Middle East conflict keep sellers in control.
body:
• Nifty 50 closed at 24,187.70 on Tuesday, down 0.21%, marking a second straight session of losses as HDFC Bank extended its selloff.
  • HDFC Bank has fallen over 7% in two sessions after reporting a sharper-than-expected decline in net interest margin for Q1 FY27, triggering analyst downgrades.
  • Brent crude hovering near $90 a barrel amid U.S.-Iran conflict and Houthi threats to Saudi Arabia is pressuring India's import bill, rupee, and corporate margins.
  • Technical analysts see key Nifty support at 24,100–24,130; a breach could trigger a slide toward 23,850, while resistance sits at 24,280–24,400.

Two-Day Selloff Deepens

Indian equity benchmarks extended their decline into a second session on Tuesday, July 21, as the fallout from HDFC Bank's disappointing quarterly earnings continued to drag on heavyweight financial stocks. The Nifty 50 fell 0.21% to close at 24,187.70, while the BSE Sensex shed 0.31% to settle at 77,470.11, according to Reuters.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=f51-_mvzrfw

The selling began on Monday when the Sensex plunged 442 points — its steepest single-day drop in weeks — after HDFC Bank, India's largest private lender by market capitalisation, reported a sharper-than-expected decline in net interest margin for the June quarter. The stock cratered 5.1% on Monday and fell another 2.1% on Tuesday, hitting a five-week low.

Axis Bank dropped 5.5% and Kotak Mahindra Bank fell 2% on Monday, making the trio the largest contributors to Nifty's losses. Investec downgraded HDFC Bank to "hold" from "buy," while Bernstein upgraded ICICI Bank to "outperform" after it bucked the trend with better-than-expected earnings.

Middle East Conflict Lifts Crude Above $88

Geopolitical risk from the Middle East compounded the selling pressure. U.S. forces struck Iran for a ninth consecutive day on Monday as concerns mounted over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, pushing Brent crude futures to $88 a barrel. By Tuesday, crude was hovering near $90.

For India, the world's third-largest crude importer, elevated oil prices are a triple threat: they fuel inflation, widen the trade deficit, and squeeze corporate margins. The Indian rupee hit a two-month low against the dollar on Monday as the risk premium on energy imports climbed.

"The banking sector has not delivered the kind of operating improvement that should normally accompany over 18% credit growth."

— Dhananjay Sinha, CEO, Systematix Group

Technical Levels to Watch

Chartists are closely watching the 24,100–24,130 zone on the Nifty 50. According to The Hindu BusinessLine's technical analysis, this support band has held through two sessions of selling and keeps the near-term bias positive. A cluster of support in the 24,200–24,100 region could anchor the index for a rebound toward 24,300–24,320 initially, with potential to reach 24,380–24,400 in coming sessions.

However, a decisive break below 24,100 would turn the near-term outlook bearish, opening the door to a slide toward 24,000 or even 23,850. On the Nifty 50 July Futures contract, resistance sits at 24,280 — a breakout above that level is needed to restore upward momentum.

Bank Nifty faces its own pressure zone. Monarch Networth Capital identified support at 56,800–57,300 and resistance at 59,800–60,300 for the week, noting that the India VIX has surged 7.33%, signalling that traders expect elevated near-term volatility amid the earnings season.

Bright Spots Amid the Gloom

The broader market showed more resilience than the blue-chip indices. Small-caps edged up 0.5% and mid-caps gained 0.3% on Tuesday, driven by stock-specific moves tied to relatively strong quarterly earnings.

"forces struck Iran for a ninth consecutive day on Monday as concerns mounted over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, pushing Brent crude futures to $88 a barrel."

UltraTech Cement rose 1.5%, building on gains after reporting a 7.4% rise in Q1 net profit to ₹2,397 crore. SBI Funds Management surged 6.2% on its market debut after a $1.03 billion IPO last week. Upstream oil producers ONGC and Oil India gained as higher crude prices improved their realisation outlook.

What to Watch This Week

The earnings calendar remains packed, with several major companies set to report Q1 results in the days ahead. The trajectory of crude oil — and any escalation or de-escalation in the U.S.-Iran confrontation — will remain the dominant macro variable. Traders should watch whether Nifty can defend the 24,100 floor; a failure to hold that level during Wednesday's session could accelerate the downside. Conversely, a break above 24,280 on futures would signal that the correction has run its course.
